diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: A submucosal cellular neoplasm composed of spindle-shaped cells with deeply eosinophilic cytoplasm, characterized by interlacing and/or intersecting fascicles or bundles, some at acute angles.

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: Areas of the tumour showing features of benign smooth muscle tumour (i.e. leiomyoma) including well-organized fascicles composed of spindle-shaped cells with uniform-appearing nuclei, some with blunt ends (cigar-shaped nuclei), and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: Fascicles appear less organized and are composed of spindle cells with mild to moderate to focally marked nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromatic nuclei, and eosinophilic cytoplasm. Despite these atypical nuclear features, mitotic figures and tumour necrosis are not present. The marked cellularity and nuclear pleomorphism are not focal but include extensive areas of the neoplasm and were therefore beyond those that might be ascribed to findings seen in symplastic leiomyomas.

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: High-magnification view shows an admixture of cells including more-differentiated cells characterized by uniform nuclei with blunt ends (cigar-shaped nuclei) and evenly dispersed nuclear chromatin admixed with less differentiated cells characterized by nuclear hyperchromasia and moderate to marked nuclear pleomorphism. All cells have brightly eosinophilic-appearing cytoplasm. Mitoses and tumour necrosis were not identified.

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: Two mitotic figures (at 3 o’clock and at 9 o’clock) are seen, but overall the mitotic count was ≤ 4 mitoses/2 mm<sup>2</sup>, with no tumour necrosis.

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: Ki-67/CD45 double staining shows a varying proliferation index, at < 5% in the better-differentiated areas of the neoplasm (right) to > 30% in the less-differentiated areas (left) (brown chromogen for Ki-67; red chromogen for CD45).

diagnosis: Smooth muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential
legend: Sinonasal mucosa showing a submucosal cellular neoplasm composed of spindle-shaped cells with deeply eosinophilic cytoplasm characterized by interlacing and/or intersecting fascicles or bundles, some at acute angles. In some areas there are features of a benign smooth muscle tumour, including well-organized fascicles composed of spindle-shaped cells with uniform-appearing nuclei, some with blunt ends (cigar-shaped nuclei) and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. In other areas, the neoplasm shows increased cellularity, less organized-appearing fascicles, hyperchromatic nuclei with mild to moderate to focally marked nuclear pleomorphism, and eosinophilic cytoplasm, but with few mitoses and no tumour necrosis.
